report.incidentSummary: Starting at 05:10 UTC (10:40 IST) on 2026-10-16, OTP login success rate dropped from ~97.4% to ~70%, accompanied by an elevated auth-service error rate (~4.5%) and user retry spikes. Investigation of internal services (auth-service, notification-service, message-queue, cache) confirmed normal system health, normal dispatch latency, and zero provider dispatch errors. The degradation is attributed to downstream SMS carrier delivery latency exceeding the shortened 240-second OTP TTL (CHG-48224), causing OTP expiration before entry, matching historical incident PIR-1602.
report.rootCauseStatement: Downstream SMS carrier delivery latency or routing delays at the external SMS provider caused OTP SMS delivery times to exceed the 240-second validity window (shortened two days prior via CHG-48224), resulting in expired OTP verification failures for approximately 25-30% of logging-in users.

hypotheses.cause: External SMS provider downstream routing degradation or carrier delivery latency delayed SMS delivery beyond the 240-second OTP TTL, causing users to enter expired codes or abandon verification.
hypotheses.rationale: Internal delivery pipelines operated normally without backlogs, queuing delays, or provider API-level rejections. Synchronous handoff to sms-provider had standard latency and zero error spikes. However, auth-service otp_success_rate dropped sharply to ~70% while otp_sent_per_min surged due to retries, a profile identical to historical carrier delivery delay incident PIR-1602, amplified by the reduction of OTP expiry from 300s to 240s in CHG-48224.

hypotheses.cause: Infrastructure upgrade CHG-48221 (log shipper v2.8 -> v3.0 on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC) caused node-level socket, memory, or CPU contention selectively degrading auth-service OTP verification handling.
hypotheses.rationale: Auth-service latency (p50 at ~60ms and p95 at ~300ms) remained completely stable before and after 04:54 UTC. Auth-service emitted zero WARN/ERROR/FATAL logs during the onset period, and OTP generation/dispatching capacity remained uninhibited.

facts.statement: On 2026-10-14 at 09:30:00 UTC, CHG-48224 decreased auth-service otp.expiry_s configuration from 300s to 240s.
At 2026-10-16 04:54:00 UTC, CHG-48221 upgraded the log shipper agent from v2.8 to v3.0 on the auth-service node pool.
Starting at 2026-10-16 05:10:00 UTC (10:40 IST), auth-service otp_success_rate fell from ~97.4% to 87.0% at 05:10, and remained depressed between 68.0% and 74.0% through 07:00 UTC.
Auth-service otp_sent_per_min increased from ~1000/min baseline to a peak of 1285/min between 05:15 and 05:25 UTC.
Auth-service latency_p50_ms (mean ~59.7ms) and latency_p95_ms (mean ~297.3ms) remained steady between 04:30 and 07:00 UTC.
Auth-service error_rate rose from baseline ~0.53% to ~4.5% starting at 05:10 UTC.
Auth-service logged zero ERROR, FATAL, or WARN logs between 04:50 and 05:30 UTC.
Notification-service error_rate remained steady at ~0.30% and sms_send_failures remained flat between 2.2 and 4.8 count/min across the entire window.
Notification-service logged 308 successful OTP SMS handoffs ('sms accepted by sms-provider') and zero SMS dispatch errors or timeouts between 04:30 and 07:00 UTC.
Notification-service latency_p95_ms remained normal between 110.8ms and 126.2ms.
Message-queue queue_depth on notifications queue stayed stable at ~83-129 messages and consumer_lag_s remained flat at ~1.6-2.5s.
Cache hit rate for the sessions keyspace remained steady at ~95% and evictions_per_min stayed flat at ~35.7 count/min.

inferences.statement: Internal components (auth-service execution, notification-service synchronous handoff, message-queue, and cache) are operating normally without degradation or internal queuing delays.

The elevation in auth-service error rate to ~4.5% corresponds to verification rejections (such as expired OTP entries or validation mismatches) rather than server-side exceptions or infrastructure failures.

Because notification-service only measures synchronous acceptance from sms-provider and does not receive asynchronous carrier delivery receipt (DLR) callbacks, downstream carrier delays are invisible in notification-service dispatch metrics.

The incident mirrors past incident PIR-1602, where SMS provider operator routing delays of 2-5 minutes pushed message delivery past the OTP expiration window, magnified by the recent TTL decrease to 240 seconds under CHG-48224.

assumptions.statement: Downstream carrier delivery latency exceeded 240 seconds for roughly 25-30% of user OTP SMS dispatches.
Notification-service does not process carrier DLR callbacks that would directly record mobile handset delivery timestamps.

confidence.rationale: Internal architectural layers (auth-service, notification-service, message-queue, cache) have been proven healthy with zero dispatch latency increases or queue lag. The symptoms and metrics closely replicate past incident PIR-1602 where carrier delivery latency exceeded OTP TTL.

recommendedActions.rationale: External provider routing latency is delaying SMS delivery past the OTP TTL.
recommendedActions.verification: Check if SMS delivery times normalize or switch to secondary SMS provider and verify auth-service otp_success_rate recovers to >95%.

recommendedActions.action: Temporarily revert CHG-48224 to increase auth-service otp.expiry_s back from 240s to 300s or 360s.
recommendedActions.rationale: Extending the OTP expiration window gives users sufficient time to receive and enter delayed SMS codes during carrier routing slowdowns.
recommendedActions.verification: Monitor auth-service otp_success_rate for an immediate recovery toward baseline (~90%+).

recommendedActions.rationale: Enables direct measurement of carrier delivery latency rather than relying solely on synchronous handoff metrics.

recommendedActions.action: Add granular OTP verification failure reason counters (expired, invalid_code, max_attempts) to auth-service metrics.

Across the entire platform on 2026-10-16, the only other recorded change was CHG-48584 at 05:25:24 UTC on kyc-service (version 1.16.0 -> 1.16.1), which occurred after the incident onset (~05:10 UTC).
Two days prior, on 2026-10-14 at 09:30:00 UTC, auth-service configuration change CHG-48224 reduced otp.expiry_s from 300s to 240s.

While the OTP expiry reduction (CHG-48224) occurred 44 hours before the incident, a shortened TTL (240s vs 300s) could amplify user login failures if SMS delivery experiences minor latency or provider delays.

Past incident PIR-2004 (2026-09-29, SEV1) had identical symptoms (OTP success dropping to 60%) caused by an SMS provider outage where sends failed at the provider, resolved by failing over to a secondary SMS provider. # Investigation report: OTP logins failing

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** budget_tool_calls · **Confidence:** 0.80 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting at 05:10 UTC (10:40 IST) on 2026-10-16, OTP login success rate dropped from ~97.4% to ~70%, accompanied by an elevated auth-service error rate (~4.5%) and user retry spikes. Investigation of internal services (auth-service, notification-service, message-queue, cache) confirmed normal system health, normal dispatch latency, and zero provider dispatch errors. The degradation is attributed to downstream SMS carrier delivery latency exceeding the shortened 240-second OTP TTL (CHG-48224), causing OTP expiration before entry, matching historical incident PIR-1602.

**Root cause:** Downstream SMS carrier delivery latency or routing delays at the external SMS provider caused OTP SMS delivery times to exceed the 240-second validity window (shortened two days prior via CHG-48224), resulting in expired OTP verification failures for approximately 25-30% of logging-in users.

## Hypotheses
1. **External SMS provider downstream routing degradation or carrier delivery latency delayed SMS delivery beyond the 240-second OTP TTL, causing users to enter expired codes or abandon verification.** — `sms-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.80, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_4, ev_7, ev_11, ev_13, ev_14, ev_16, ev_17, ev_19, ev_21, ev_24, ev_25, ev_26, ev_27, ev_28, ev_29, ev_30, ev_32, ev_33, ev_34, ev_36] · Contradicting: none
   - Internal delivery pipelines operated normally without backlogs, queuing delays, or provider API-level rejections. Synchronous handoff to sms-provider had standard latency and zero error spikes. However, auth-service otp_success_rate dropped sharply to ~70% while otp_sent_per_min surged due to retries, a profile identical to historical carrier delivery delay incident PIR-1602, amplified by the reduction of OTP expiry from 300s to 240s in CHG-48224.
2. **Infrastructure upgrade CHG-48221 (log shipper v2.8 -> v3.0 on auth-service node pool at 04:54 UTC) caused node-level socket, memory, or CPU contention selectively degrading auth-service OTP verification handling.** — `auth-service`, infrastructure_failure, confidence 0.10, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_2, ev_5, ev_29, ev_36] · Contradicting: [ev_11, ev_22, ev_27, ev_34, ev_35]
   - Auth-service latency (p50 at ~60ms and p95 at ~300ms) remained completely stable before and after 04:54 UTC. Auth-service emitted zero WARN/ERROR/FATAL logs during the onset period, and OTP generation/dispatching capacity remained uninhibited.

## Facts
- On 2026-10-14 at 09:30:00 UTC, CHG-48224 decreased auth-service otp.expiry_s configuration from 300s to 240s. [ev_7]
- At 2026-10-16 04:54:00 UTC, CHG-48221 upgraded the log shipper agent from v2.8 to v3.0 on the auth-service node pool. [ev_2, ev_5]
- Starting at 2026-10-16 05:10:00 UTC (10:40 IST), auth-service otp_success_rate fell from ~97.4% to 87.0% at 05:10, and remained depressed between 68.0% and 74.0% through 07:00 UTC. [ev_4, ev_33]
- Auth-service otp_sent_per_min increased from ~1000/min baseline to a peak of 1285/min between 05:15 and 05:25 UTC. [ev_11]
- Auth-service latency_p50_ms (mean ~59.7ms) and latency_p95_ms (mean ~297.3ms) remained steady between 04:30 and 07:00 UTC. [ev_27, ev_34]
- Auth-service error_rate rose from baseline ~0.53% to ~4.5% starting at 05:10 UTC. [ev_29, ev_36]
- Auth-service logged zero ERROR, FATAL, or WARN logs between 04:50 and 05:30 UTC. [ev_22, ev_35]
- Notification-service error_rate remained steady at ~0.30% and sms_send_failures remained flat between 2.2 and 4.8 count/min across the entire window. [ev_13, ev_19, ev_21, ev_24]
- Notification-service logged 308 successful OTP SMS handoffs ('sms accepted by sms-provider') and zero SMS dispatch errors or timeouts between 04:30 and 07:00 UTC. [ev_14, ev_16, ev_18, ev_37]
- Notification-service latency_p95_ms remained normal between 110.8ms and 126.2ms. [ev_28]
- Message-queue queue_depth on notifications queue stayed stable at ~83-129 messages and consumer_lag_s remained flat at ~1.6-2.5s. [ev_17, ev_25]
- Cache hit rate for the sessions keyspace remained steady at ~95% and evictions_per_min stayed flat at ~35.7 count/min. [ev_6, ev_8]

## Inferences
- Internal components (auth-service execution, notification-service synchronous handoff, message-queue, and cache) are operating normally without degradation or internal queuing delays. [ev_6, ev_8, ev_14, ev_17, ev_19, ev_25, ev_27, ev_28, ev_34]
- The elevation in auth-service error rate to ~4.5% corresponds to verification rejections (such as expired OTP entries or validation mismatches) rather than server-side exceptions or infrastructure failures. [ev_4, ev_22, ev_27, ev_29, ev_35, ev_36]
- Because notification-service only measures synchronous acceptance from sms-provider and does not receive asynchronous carrier delivery receipt (DLR) callbacks, downstream carrier delays are invisible in notification-service dispatch metrics. [ev_14, ev_15, ev_20]
- The incident mirrors past incident PIR-1602, where SMS provider operator routing delays of 2-5 minutes pushed message delivery past the OTP expiration window, magnified by the recent TTL decrease to 240 seconds under CHG-48224. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_7, ev_11]

## Assumptions
- Downstream carrier delivery latency exceeded 240 seconds for roughly 25-30% of user OTP SMS dispatches.
- Notification-service does not process carrier DLR callbacks that would directly record mobile handset delivery timestamps.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-14 15:00 IST (09:30 UTC)** CHG-48224 applied, reducing auth-service otp.expiry_s configuration from 300s to 240s. [ev_7]
- **2026-10-16 10:24 IST (04:54 UTC)** CHG-48221 applied, upgrading log shipper agent v2.8 to v3.0 on auth-service node pool. [ev_2, ev_5]
- **2026-10-16 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC)** Auth-service otp_success_rate drops from ~97.4% to 87.0%, and error_rate begins increasing from ~0.53% to 2.16%. [ev_4, ev_29, ev_33]
- **2026-10-16 10:45 - 10:55 IST (05:15 - 05:25 UTC)** Auth-service otp_success_rate falls to ~70-72%; otp_sent_per_min surges to 1285/min as users trigger retries. [ev_4, ev_11, ev_33]
- **2026-10-16 11:20 IST (05:50 UTC)** On-call SRE reports SEV1 incident INC-6097 citing OTP login failures. [ev_4]
- **2026-10-16 12:30 IST (07:00 UTC)** Otp_success_rate remains depressed at ~68% and auth-service error_rate remains at ~4.5% while notification-service and queue metrics remain baseline. [ev_4, ev_17, ev_19, ev_25, ev_28, ev_29, ev_33]

## Confidence
0.80: Internal architectural layers (auth-service, notification-service, message-queue, cache) have been proven healthy with zero dispatch latency increases or queue lag. The symptoms and metrics closely replicate past incident PIR-1602 where carrier delivery latency exceeded OTP TTL.

## Gaps
- Carrier delivery receipts (DLR) and delivery receipt latency metrics are not collected by notification-service. (impact: Direct timestamps of SMS handset receipt are unavailable from internal observability tools, requiring inference from verification patterns and provider status.)
- Auth-service verification error breakdown (e.g. expired vs invalid code) was not directly queryable from logs due to log level filtering. (impact: Inability to quantitatively partition the exact proportion of expired OTP errors versus incorrect user entries.)

## Tool failures
- query_metrics {"service":"notification-service","metric":"delivery_receipt_latency_s","from":"2026-10-16T04:30:00.000Z","to":"2026-10-16T07:00:00.000Z","aggregation":"avg"}: invalid_input: service notification-service has no metric "delivery_receipt_latency_s". Available: error_rate, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, push_send_failures, request_rate, sms_send_failures (1 attempts)
- query_metrics {"service":"notification-service","metric":"queue_lag","from":"2026-10-16T04:30:00.000Z","to":"2026-10-16T07:00:00.000Z","aggregation":"avg"}: invalid_input: service notification-service has no metric "queue_lag". Available: error_rate, latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, push_send_failures, request_rate, sms_send_failures (1 attempts)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Engage SMS provider support to report operator routing latency and consider failing over to secondary SMS provider as done in PIR-2004. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_33]
  - Why: External provider routing latency is delaying SMS delivery past the OTP TTL.
  - Verify: Check if SMS delivery times normalize or switch to secondary SMS provider and verify auth-service otp_success_rate recovers to >95%.
- **[now]** Temporarily revert CHG-48224 to increase auth-service otp.expiry_s back from 240s to 300s or 360s. [ev_4, ev_7, ev_33]
  - Why: Extending the OTP expiration window gives users sufficient time to receive and enter delayed SMS codes during carrier routing slowdowns.
  - Verify: Monitor auth-service otp_success_rate for an immediate recovery toward baseline (~90%+).
- **[next]** Implement asynchronous carrier delivery receipt (DLR) callback tracking and telemetry within notification-service. [ev_15, ev_20]
  - Why: Enables direct measurement of carrier delivery latency rather than relying solely on synchronous handoff metrics.
  - Verify: Confirm presence of delivery_receipt_latency_s metric on notification-service dashboards.
- **[later]** Add granular OTP verification failure reason counters (expired, invalid_code, max_attempts) to auth-service metrics. [ev_4, ev_29]
  - Why: Allows instantaneous distinction between expired OTPs and bad user input during future login degradation incidents.
  - Verify: Verify new metric labels appear under auth-service verification metrics.

Cited evidence: ev_2, ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_7, ev_8, ev_11, ev_13, ev_14, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17, ev_18, ev_19, ev_20, ev_21, ev_22, ev_24, ev_25, ev_26, ev_27, ev_28, ev_29, ev_30, ev_32, ev_33, ev_34, ev_35, ev_36, ev_37
